claim_as_stated: Holding census strata fixed is the right measure of what the census bought
validation_result: partially confirmed: design-based logic is right (a fully enumerated stratum has no sampling variance, and the repo method wrongly resamples it with replacement), and old and new runs fix the same kinds of strata; but the variant still omits FPC on partly sampled strata and measures only FY2023–24 finite-population sampling error
interpretation_challenge: If the target is a typical-year share (superpopulation view), census strata still carry year-to-year variance that fpc0 drops. Treat the census-corrected CI as sampling error for FY2023–24 only; quote the allocation envelope beside it.

claim_as_stated: 1h−1d−1e moves −0.14 pt against −0.35 on 1h; candidate cause (health ≥$100m carry large 1d/1e) untested
validation_result: partially confirmed: the study's candidate is supported by validator decomposition. In non-certainty ≥$100m strata the census raised the weighted 1h denominator by $26.97bn (146.96→173.93bn) but the 1a+1b+1c+1f denominator by only $3.37bn (76.76→80.13bn); $22.7bn of the rise is line 1e and $0.9bn line 1d; health alone adds $20.5bn of 1h ($11.4bn of it 1e)
exact_values_found: counterfactual: new sample with the ≥$100m non-certainty band held at old values gives 9.17% (1h) and 13.68% (1h−1d−1e)
interpretation_challenge: The ≥$100m band explains essentially all of the 1h fall and about 0.10 of the 0.14-point fall on 1h−1d−1e: the recipients it adds are largely government-funded, so they enlarge 1h much more than the private-contributions basis.
